figures.caption: Figure 3: Class distribution across the first 20 clients under pathological (shard-based) partitioning on CIFAR-10. Each client contains samples from a limited subset of classes, demonstrating extreme label skew.

Table 1: Performance Comparison under Extreme Heterogeneity (Dirichlet 𝛼 = 0.1). All values are accuracy (%). Results are reported as mean ± standard deviation (0.5–0.9%). FedPrism consistently achieves superior local personalization while maintaining competitive global performance.

Table 2: Results for Pathological Non-IID Setting on SVHN. Global models struggle to converge or suffer from negative transfer, while FedPrism achieves high personalization. Results are reported as mean ± standard deviation (0.5–0.9%).
Figure 1: Overview of the FedPrism framework illustrating dynamic clustering, soft assignment, and the Global–Cluster–Personal (GCP) model decomposition within the federated learning pipeline.
Figure 2: Class distribution across the first 20 clients under Dirichlet partitioning with 𝛼 = 0.1 on CIFAR-10.
